falsePositiveProof.argument: For m=existing.length and n=newCount, preferKeep partitions existing, hence has length m. Creation requires n>m; removal requires max(m-n,0)>0, hence n<m. No invocation can satisfy both. Pinned tier counts are 1,2,4.

findings.notes: The account update at process:58 commits before the transaction batches at process:93 (transactions.ts:2081). The window is real. The transactions queue retries jobs three times (transactions.config.ts:14), BaseProcessor.handle rethrows retryable failures (base.ts:245-246), and shouldProcess defaults to true (base.ts:319-321). Retrying overwrites the same account and transaction base values; there is no increment or completion guard skipping the failed batch. Classify as a retried recomputation job, not an impossible window or a guaranteed permanent inconsistency. Exhausted retries or non-retryable errors can still leave stale derived values.

findings.notes: Upgrade/downgrade writes each kept subscription at webhook.ts:287 and each linked workspace at :299 in Promise.all on the root DB, without one transaction. For an existing linked slot, one UPDATE can commit and the other fail, leaving subscription entitlements and workspace plan inconsistent. Promise.all does not roll back completed siblings. HTTP 500 handling in withApiLogging is not durable compensation or a guaranteed redelivery contract. This is the already reported inner-handler window at 574be59f041f0e7e, exposed at the default export, not a new independent bug.

findings.notes: The first insertion is reached only through createAndLinkSlots when newCount > existing.length (webhook.ts:303-314). The later removed-subscription UPDATE requires slotsToRemove.length > 0 (:317-329). preferKeep is the concatenation of the truthy and falsy referenceId partitions of existing (:277-280), so its length equals existing.length. With nonnegative tier counts 1, 2 or 4, slotsToRemove = preferKeep.slice(newCount) can be nonempty only when newCount < existing.length. Both conditions cannot hold in one invocation. The same contradiction holds in the migrate branch. No real partial-state window corresponds to this pair.

findings.notes: createAndLinkSlots can execute both slot INSERTs: available.length > 0 at :60 creates slots at :61, autoLinked becomes available.length at :90, and count-autoLinked > 0 creates the remainder at :97. For example, growing from one existing slot to tier 3 (four slots) requests count=3; one eligible owned workspace gives available.length=1 and remaining=2. The first INSERT commits independently of linking and of the remainder INSERT. A failure can leave an incomplete or partly linked allocation; no encompassing transaction or cleanup undoes it. This is the same helper window as 11727d753731af8a at a default-export context.

findings.notes: importSingleBoard commits cardRepo.bulkCreate at import.ts:382 before cardActivityRepo.bulkCreate at :406. The card transaction ends in card.repo.ts before the independent activity INSERT. A failed activity write leaves committed cards without creation activity and aborts the remaining per-board import. Promise.allSettled (:536) only records the rejection; :561 updates the import status, not the missing data. A rerun allocates fresh IDs and creates another board (:317-326), rather than repairing this one. This is an existing importSingleBoard window at 2aadc5212a97547b, now reached through the captured callback.

findings.notes: boardRepo.create commits the board and creator membership in its own transaction (board.repo.ts:639-662), before labelRepo.bulkCreate inserts labels at import.ts:349. A board with at least one label takes both operations; a failure between leaves a visible, incomplete imported board. There is no outer transaction or per-board cleanup; allSettled and the final import-status update cannot undo the committed board, and a retry generates a new public ID (:317). This duplicates the already reported f322f5de643c442a window at a caller context.

findings.notes: The exported sendMessages calls the provider sender at broadcasts/activities.ts:360, waits for sends at :368, and only then publishes delivery events with submitBatch at :413. The retry policy is explicit (broadcastWorkflowV2.ts:154-160), but the resend guard getUnmessagedUsers/searchDeliveries (:176-186) depends on the very delivery events absent after a send/publish failure. Thus retry can resend an already delivered message; a deterministic tracking messageId does not make the provider call idempotent. This follows the more recent source-grounded true-positive judgment 4b0058e6a225b154. The older 8af63194255c32d4 intended-risk label disagrees; it is preserved and flagged for human review. This is not a new independent bug or a runtime-confirmed duplicate delivery.

findings.notes: sendMessageV2 calls sender at userWorkflow/activities.ts:259 and publishes submitTrack at :385, so the delivery/recording window is real. The journey explicitly configures per-node retryCount (userWorkflow.ts:948-958); the activity distinguishes final attempts and returns a skipped result after exhaustion (:270-300), and events reuse the messageId (:244-252,:375-385; apps/track.ts:25). Retain the existing intended-risk interpretation for this retry-aware, at-least-once journey activity rather than asserting a new bug without a stricter delivery contract. This does not establish provider-side deduplication or exactly-once delivery. The existing KP01 auditor/labeler disagreement remains open; the new export context duplicates ece472399ebf7efb and 0a33bc81d8b3fa98.
